verdict.rationale: Docs describe a dedicated 'cloud workspace' feature where agents run in isolated sandboxes that 'spin up in seconds' and 'keep working after you close your laptop,' can test repos/run builds unattended, and continue processing PR checks while 'asleep' (conductor-docs-20, conductor-docs-17, conductor-docs-11, conductor-docs-13). However, community reports describe the core product as creating an isolated git worktree locally rather than a cloud container, contrasting it with Codex's cloud sandbox (conductor-comm-17, conductor-comm-6), suggesting the cloud-isolation capability may be a newer/optional layer rather than the default experience. Missing for 10: independent hands-on verification that background cloud tasks are fully isolated/persistent, and clarity on whether cloud workspaces are the default vs. opt-in given local-worktree-first community accounts.
